acronyms.expansion: Systems, Applications, Products in Data Processing
acronyms.blurb: The full name of the company behind your daily BTP adventures. Founded in Walldorf, 1972.
SAP's unified cloud platform for building, extending, and integrating business applications. The successor to SAP Cloud Platform (SCP).
The former name of SAP BTP (deprecated 2021). You'll still see SCP in older tutorials and Stack Overflow answers.
SAP's cloud-based Identity Provider (IdP) on BTP. Handles authentication for SAP apps and custom services via SAML 2.0 and OIDC.

beats.kasimir: Ah, a fresh student! Before we write a single line of CDS, let's settle the most fundamental questions: who runs this show, and what platform are we on?

beats.answer: Systems, Applications, Products in Data Processing
beats.kasimirRight: Correct! Even I know who signs my cat food invoices. 🐱
beats.kasimirWrong: SAP = Systems, Applications, Products in Data Processing. It's literally on the letterhead!

beats.kasimirRight: BTP — the cloud with a view from Walldorf! Nicely done. ☁️
beats.kasimirWrong: BTP = SAP Business Technology Platform. The "T" is Technology, not Transaction.

beats.kasimirRight: SCP — the old BTP. Nostalgia is allowed. 📜
beats.kasimirWrong: SCP = SAP Cloud Platform, the predecessor to BTP. History matters in enterprise software!

beats.kasimirRight: IAS — the bouncer of the SAP cloud. Excellent! 🚪
beats.kasimirWrong: IAS = SAP Identity Authentication Service. It's the IdP, not just any authorization layer.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered SAP, BTP, SCP, IAS. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: SAP's framework for building cloud-native business applications using CDS, Node.js, and Java. The backbone of tutorials-ims.
SAP's browser-based IDE on BTP, built on VS Code Open Source. The recommended tool for CAP, Fiori, and ABAP Cloud development.
A bundle of tools, libraries, and documentation for building on a platform. SAP Cloud SDK adds BTP destinations, resilience, and type-safe OData clients.
A defined contract that lets software components talk to each other. SAP publishes thousands of APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub (api.sap.com).

beats.kasimir: Now we're cooking! CAP is where the magic happens. Let me introduce you to my favourite framework — and no, I'm not biased just because it's named after something a professor wears.

beats.kasimirRight: CAP! You've earned a treat. My whole world runs on CAP. 🐾
beats.kasimirWrong: CAP = SAP Cloud Application Programming Model. CDS, Node.js, Java — it's all in there.

beats.kasimirRight: BAS — where humans write the code that Kasimir reviews. Well played! 💻
beats.kasimirWrong: BAS = SAP Business Application Studio — the cloud IDE on BTP, not a backend system.

beats.kasimirRight: SDK — the box of LEGO bricks every developer loves. Exactly right! 🧰
beats.kasimirWrong: SDK = Software Development Kit. Not "Service Deployment" anything.

beats.kasimirRight: API — the handshake of the cloud world. I knew you'd get this one! 🤝
beats.kasimirWrong: API = Application Programming Interface. The "P" is Programming, not Process.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered CAP, BAS, SDK, API. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: SAP's deployment artefact format for BTP. A single `.mtar` archive bundles multiple modules (backend, UI, DB) and wires up service bindings automatically.
A BTP service that sends real-time alerts about application events to email, Slack, or custom webhooks. Used in tutorials-ims for operational monitoring.
SAP's SaaS business intelligence platform for dashboards, planning, and predictive analytics. Lives on BTP.
A cross-platform toolkit for building native-looking SAP mobile apps that work offline. Based on a metadata-driven approach — no separate iOS/Android code.

beats.kasimir: Congratulations — you've built a CAP app! Now how do you actually ship it? MTA archives, alert services, analytics clouds — the operational layer awaits.

beats.kasimirRight: MTA — one package to rule them all! Purrfectly correct. 📦
beats.kasimirWrong: MTA = Multi-Target Application. It bundles all your BTP modules into one deployable archive.

beats.kasimirRight: ANS — the smoke alarm of your BTP app. Alert! You're correct! 🚨
beats.kasimirWrong: ANS = SAP Alert Notification Service. It notifies, alerts, and generally keeps you from sleeping.

beats.kasimirRight: SAC — where data becomes pretty pictures! Right on target. 📊
beats.kasimirWrong: SAC = SAP Analytics Cloud. Dashboards, planning, predictions — all in the cloud.

beats.kasimirRight: MDK — go mobile! Even I have a paw-friendly app. Great answer! 📱
beats.kasimirWrong: MDK = SAP Mobile Development Kit. Cross-platform, metadata-driven, and furiously offline-capable.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered MTA, ANS, SAC, MDK. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: CAP's universal declarative language for data models and service definitions. Also powers S/4HANA views. The backbone of everything in CAP.
CDS models compiled to a compact JSON representation (pronounced "Season"). The runtime format CAP uses internally — generated from CDL source files.
The human-readable source syntax you write in `.cds` files — entities, services, annotations. Compiles to CSN for runtime use.
The SQL-like query language for CAP: `SELECT.from(Books).where(...)`. Type-safe, composable, and database-agnostic. Part of the `cds.ql` API.

beats.kasimir: CDS is not one thing — it's a whole language family. CSN, CDL, CQL… I collect acronyms the way others collect stamps. Let's unpack them.

beats.kasimirRight: CDS — the language I dream in! You've clearly been reading the docs. 📚
beats.kasimirWrong: CDS = Core Data Services — SAP's universal modeling language. Not "Cloud" anything.

beats.kasimirRight: CSN — like JSON Schema but for full entity-relationship models. Season greetings! 🎄
beats.kasimirWrong: CSN = Core Schema Notation, pronounced "Season". It's the JSON form of your CDS models.

beats.kasimirRight: CDL — what you write, CSN is what the machine reads. You're fluent! ✍️
beats.kasimirWrong: CDL = CDS Definition Language. The .cds files you write are CDL; they compile down to CSN.

beats.kasimirRight: CQL — SELECT * FROM correct_answers! Top marks. 🐱‍💻
beats.kasimirWrong: CQL = CDS Query Language — the SELECT.from(...) syntax in `cds.ql`. Never write raw SQL!

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered CDS, CSN, CDL, CQL. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: An OASIS standard REST-based protocol for CRUD APIs with query capabilities ($filter, $expand, $top…). All CAP services can be served as OData V4.
SAP's recommended framework for building Fiori apps and OData services on ABAP. Uses CDS views, behavior definitions, and service bindings.
The architectural style behind most web APIs: stateless HTTP, resources as URLs, verbs as HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE). OData is a RESTful protocol.
A software tool that combines code editor, debugger, and build tools in one UI. SAP's cloud IDE is BAS; locally VS Code + CDS extension is the go-to.

beats.kasimir: Every API speaks a language. OData, REST, RAP — the protocols that let your app talk to the world. Put on your headphones; it's time for a multilingual lesson.

beats.kasimirRight: OData — the protocol that makes SAP APIs queryable from Excel. Impressive! 📡
beats.kasimirWrong: OData = Open Data Protocol (OASIS standard). Think REST + $filter + $expand — pure power.

beats.kasimirRight: RAP — the CAP of the ABAP world! You're now officially bilingual. 🎓
beats.kasimirWrong: RAP = ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model. It's to ABAP what CAP is to Node.js/Java.

beats.kasimirRight: REST — the law of the web land. Stateless, resourceful, correct! 🌐
beats.kasimirWrong: REST = Representational State Transfer (Roy Fielding, 2000). Every web API architect owes him a coffee.

beats.kasimirRight: IDE — where the magic happens before the bug report! You knew it. 🖥️
beats.kasimirWrong: IDE = Integrated Development Environment. VS Code + CDS extension = one happy IDE.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered OData, RAP, REST, IDE. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: The web shell that hosts SAP Fiori apps as tiles in a unified homepage. Handles navigation, routing, and user personalization across all Fiori apps.
SAP's enterprise JavaScript UI framework (based on OpenUI5). Delivers Fiori-ready components, Horizon theme, and OData V4 model binding out of the box.
SAP's asynchronous integration-test framework for UI5/Fiori apps. Tests page objects and UI flows without flakiness, running inside the browser.
A text-based tool for interacting with software. CAP provides `cds` CLI; BTP has `btp`; CF has `cf`. Together they're the developer's Swiss army knife.

beats.kasimir: A developer without tools is just someone staring at a blank screen. FLP, UI5, OPA, CLI — the toolkit that turns ideas into shipped features.

beats.kasimirRight: FLP — the tile garden where Fiori apps bloom! Nailed it. 🏡
beats.kasimirWrong: FLP = SAP Fiori Launchpad — the shell that tiles up your Fiori apps in one place.

beats.kasimirRight: UI5 — the framework behind every Fiori face! Stylishly correct. 🎨
beats.kasimirWrong: UI5 = SAPUI5 — SAP's enterprise JavaScript framework. OpenUI5 is its open-source twin.

beats.kasimirRight: OPA — the test cat catches every bug! Acceptably correct. 🧪
beats.kasimirWrong: OPA = One Page Acceptance Test Framework — UI5's built-in asynchronous integration test library.

beats.kasimirRight: CLI — where humans type furiously and things actually happen! Correct! ⌨️
beats.kasimirWrong: CLI = Command-Line Interface. `cds watch`, `btp login`, `cf push` — all CLI commands.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered FLP, UI5, OPA, CLI. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: SAP's in-memory relational database. Processes analytical and transactional workloads simultaneously ("HTAP"). The default production database for CAP apps on BTP.
A SAP HANA feature that manages database artefacts (tables, views, procedures) in isolated, versioned containers. CAP uses HDI containers for all HANA deployments.
A HANA feature for querying remote data sources (S/4HANA, Oracle, etc.) as virtual tables — without physically moving the data. Federation without ETL.
HANA's data integration layer: real-time replication, batch loading, and transformation from heterogeneous sources using Data Provisioning Agents.

beats.kasimir: SAP HANA — high-performance, in-memory, and living in its own acronym universe. HDI, SDA, SDI… even I need a map sometimes.

beats.kasimirRight: HANA — in-memory, in-the-cloud, and in your heart. Right answer! 💾
beats.kasimirWrong: HANA = High-performance ANalytic Appliance. The capital letters in the middle are the clue!

beats.kasimirRight: HDI — HANA Deployment Infrastructure. Container-ised perfection! 📦
beats.kasimirWrong: HDI = HANA Deployment Infrastructure. It's the container system that keeps your DB artefacts isolated.

beats.kasimirRight: SDA — federation without migration! Your HANA knowledge is sharp. 🔗
beats.kasimirWrong: SDA = SAP HANA Smart Data Access — virtual tables pointing at remote sources. No data movement needed.

beats.kasimirRight: SDI — data flows like water to a thirsty cat! Correct! 🌊
beats.kasimirWrong: SDI = SAP HANA Smart Data Integration. Real-time replication + transformations via DP Agents.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered HANA, HDI, SDA, SDI. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: The former name for SAP Integration Suite's cloud integration capability. Still widely used in docs and project names. Handles message routing and transformation between systems.
SAP's cloud data warehouse solution, rebranded as SAP Datasphere in 2023. Provides data modelling, integration, and analytics on a single platform.
The standard language for relational databases. In CAP, you should use CQL (CDS Query Language) instead of raw SQL — but HANA's SQL dialect is what runs under the hood.
SAP's framework for extracting data from S/4HANA and ECC sources into analytics or integration platforms. Exposes CDS views, BW extractors, and SLT as replication sources.

beats.kasimir: Data doesn't just sit still. CPI, DWC, SQL, ODP — the connectors and extractors that keep data flowing where it needs to go.

beats.kasimirRight: CPI — connecting the dots since before it was called Integration Suite! 🔌
beats.kasimirWrong: CPI = SAP Cloud Platform Integration — now part of SAP Integration Suite, but the name persists.

beats.kasimirRight: DWC — now Datasphere but the acronym lives on. Historically accurate! 📐
beats.kasimirWrong: DWC = SAP Data Warehouse Cloud — rebranded to SAP Datasphere in 2023 but DWC still appears everywhere.

beats.kasimirRight: SQL — the granddaddy of data languages. CAP wraps it, but knowing it never hurts! ✅
beats.kasimirWrong: SQL = Structured Query Language. Use CQL in CAP code, but SQL is what HANA actually runs.

beats.kasimirRight: ODP — the SAP data extraction expressway! Spot on. 🚂
beats.kasimirWrong: ODP = Operational Data Provisioning — SAP's framework for exporting data from ERP systems to analytics.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered CPI, DWC, SQL, ODP. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: The classic data pipeline pattern: extract from source, transform (cleanse/enrich), load into target. Used in SAP Data Services, BW, and Datasphere pipelines.
The "HDB" prefix appears across HANA tooling: `hdbsql` (CLI SQL client), `.hdbtable` artefact files, and `@sap/hana-client` (the Node.js driver).
The SQL subset for defining database structures: CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP. In CAP, CDS handles DDL generation automatically from your models.
A database column type for storing large binary (BLOB) or text (CLOB) data. SAP HANA supports LOBs natively; CAP uses raw `db.run()` to read them (locators expire on SELECT).

beats.kasimir: Time to get into the weeds: ETL pipelines, HDB artefacts, DDL, and the dreaded LOB column. Grab a coffee — or a warm saucer of milk.

beats.kasimirRight: ETL — the cat-nap to data-warehouse pipeline of legend! Extract correct answer, +1. 📥
beats.kasimirWrong: ETL = Extract, Transform, Load — the three-step dance every data warehouse knows by heart.

beats.kasimirRight: HDB — you'll see this prefix everywhere in HANA-land. Well spotted! 🐾
beats.kasimirWrong: HDB = SAP HANA Database — the prefix behind hdbsql, .hdbtable files, and the Node.js driver.

beats.kasimirRight: DDL — CREATE TABLE? More like CREATE SUCCESS. Correct! 🏗️
beats.kasimirWrong: DDL = Data Definition Language — CREATE, ALTER, DROP. CAP generates it from CDS; you rarely write it directly.

beats.kasimirRight: LOB — big data in a small column. Don't mix it with a CDS QL query! Correct! 📦
beats.kasimirWrong: LOB = Large Object (BLOB/CLOB) — in HANA, never SELECT a LOB alongside metadata in one CDS QL query.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered ETL, HDB, DDL, LOB. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.expansion: Extended Services for User Account and Authorization
acronyms.blurb: SAP BTP's OAuth 2.0 authorization service (also called "Authorization and Trust Management Service"). Manages roles, scopes, and JWT tokens for CAP apps.
Cloud Foundry's open-source OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect server. SAP's XSUAA is a proprietary extension of UAA, adding BTP-specific scopes and role collections.
Log in once, access everything. SAP IAS federates identity to BTP, SAP S/4HANA, and third-party apps so users don't need separate passwords per system.
A compact, URL-safe token format (RFC 7519) for conveying claims between parties. BTP uses JWTs to carry XSUAA scopes and user info between services.

beats.kasimir: Security is not optional, and neither is this lesson. XSUAA, UAA, SSO, JWT — the alphabet soup that keeps your data from becoming everyone's data.

beats.answer: Extended Services for User Account and Authorization
beats.kasimirRight: XSUAA — the gatekeeper with too many letters! You cracked it. 🔑
beats.kasimirWrong: XSUAA = Extended Services for User Account and Authorization. Every CAP prod app uses it.

beats.kasimirRight: UAA — the open-source core under XSUAA! Cloud Foundry heritage. Well done. 🦊
beats.kasimirWrong: UAA = User Account and Authentication — the CF OAuth server that XSUAA is built on top of.

beats.kasimirRight: SSO — one password to rule them all! You didn't even need to log in twice. 🔓
beats.kasimirWrong: SSO = Single Sign-On. Sign in once, use everything — Kasimir only has to remember one paw-print.

beats.kasimirRight: JWT — the travel passport of the cloud! Header.Payload.Signature, correct! 🛂
beats.kasimirWrong: JWT = JSON Web Token (RFC 7519). Three base64-encoded parts: header.payload.signature.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered XSUAA, UAA, SSO, JWT. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: A system that authenticates users and issues identity tokens. SAP IAS is a BTP Identity Provider. Corporate IdPs (Azure AD, Okta) can be federated into IAS.
Requiring ≥2 verification methods (password + OTP, biometric, hardware key). SAP IAS supports MFA for BTP admin and application users.
The cryptographic protocol that secures HTTPS connections (successor to SSL). All BTP endpoints use TLS; CAP enforces it in production profiles automatically.
A list specifying which users or roles can perform which operations on a resource. In CAP, `@restrict` annotations compile to XSUAA role-scope checks, implementing ACL logic.

beats.kasimir: Logging in is just the start. IDP, MFA, TLS, ACL — the layers that stop the wrong people from doing the wrong things.

beats.kasimirRight: IDP — the trust anchor of the auth chain. You clearly trust your acronym knowledge! 🏛️
beats.kasimirWrong: IDP = Identity Provider — the system that says "yes, that IS Kasimir" during login.

beats.kasimirRight: MFA — two factors better than one! Twice as secure, half as convenient. Correct! 🔐
beats.kasimirWrong: MFA = Multi-Factor Authentication. Password + something else — a password alone is so last century.

beats.kasimirRight: TLS — the invisible shield on every HTTPS call. Lock-tight answer! 🔒
beats.kasimirWrong: TLS = Transport Layer Security — the "S" in HTTPS. SSL is the deprecated predecessor.

beats.kasimirRight: ACL — the velvet rope of data security! Access granted to correct answers. 🚦
beats.kasimirWrong: ACL = Access Control List. In CAP terms, it's what `@restrict` annotations enforce via XSUAA scopes.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered IDP, MFA, TLS, ACL. Kasimir approves. 🐱

acronyms.blurb: Software that integrates core business processes (finance, HR, supply chain). SAP S/4HANA is the flagship ERP; it's why CAP and BTP exist — to extend and integrate ERP.
A framework (and SAP product family) for managing audit, risk, and regulatory requirements. SAP GRC integrates with S/4HANA to automate access controls and policy enforcement.
A BTP service (`@cap-js/ams`) providing policy-based authorization for CAP applications via the `@ams` CDS annotation. An alternative to pure XSUAA role checks.
Assigning permissions to roles, then roles to users — rather than granting permissions directly. XSUAA role collections implement RBAC for BTP apps.

beats.kasimir: The business side of security: ERP context, GRC compliance, AMS policies, and the RBAC model that ties it all together.

beats.kasimirRight: ERP — the reason SAP exists and why your paycheck clears. Exactly right! 💼
beats.kasimirWrong: ERP = Enterprise Resource Planning — the big system that runs the business. S/4HANA is SAP's ERP.

beats.kasimirRight: GRC — keeping the auditors happy since forever. Correctly compliant answer! 📋
beats.kasimirWrong: GRC = Governance, Risk, and Compliance. A whole SAP product family dedicated to keeping regulators at bay.

beats.kasimirRight: AMS — policy-based, fine-grained, and very grown-up authorization. Nailed it! 🏆
beats.kasimirWrong: AMS = SAP Authorization Management Service — the `@cap-js/ams` plugin for fine-grained policy authorization.

beats.kasimirRight: RBAC — roles for the role, access for the few. Permission granted! 🎖️
beats.kasimirWrong: RBAC = Role-Based Access Control. XSUAA role collections ARE the RBAC mechanism in BTP.

beats.kasimir: Lesson complete! You've mastered ERP, GRC, AMS, RBAC. Kasimir approves. 🐱
